Old British nurse here (ex-NHS). There are several reasons why this might be but the most common for you is likely that at the start of your period, an extra large amount of prostaglandin is released to start the uterine shedding. This causes those 'labour pains' cramps that can also affect the thighs and back, and also nausea, faintness and cold sweats. Your age - and that is doesn't happen every period - is quite diagnostic (but see your gyny if you're really worried or have other symptoms). What to do? 1) Mirena. 2) If you can reliably predict your period then, starting 2 days before you're due on, take an NSAID like Ibuprofen, say 200mg every 6-8 hours. As soon as you feel the first faint twinge of period pain or start bleeding - whichever comes first - take 400mgs immediately (even if you've recently taken 200mgs as you can safely go up 800mgs occasionally). You'll need to keep these tablets and some water with you at all times - coffee is better as gets it into your system faster but you don't want to waste even a minute getting those tablets down you once you know you've started, as these pains can go from 1 to 10 in a few short minutes. This advice is based upon what British GPs advise, and which they gave me as I also suffered this for years. I wish you luck, if you need any more info I'll be happy to recommend links etc.
